entries.source_title: Difference between subjects, objects and pronouns - Grammar Point
entries.evidence: Defines subject, direct/indirect object and replacement pronoun using Nora's call; assessment identifies the subject and selects objects.

entries.source_title: Using French Stress Pronouns in compound subjects and objects (unlike English)
entries.evidence: Joined subject and object examples both use stressed forms; items require toi after a preposition and moi within a subject.

entries.source_title: Using le/la/l'/les = it/him/her/them (French Direct Object Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Teaches the complete third-person direct-object series, elision and French-direct verbs such as chercher and remercier.

entries.source_title: Using lui/leur = him or her/them (French Indirect Object Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Contrasts indirect lui/leur with direct pronouns and the penser à stressed-pronoun exception.

entries.source_title: Position of French Object Pronouns - with simple tenses
entries.evidence: Shows before-verb placement in simple tenses and requires rewriting a full present-tense sentence.

entries.source_title: Position of French Object Pronouns - with infinitives
entries.evidence: Separates an infinitive's object from the first verb's object; transformations assess both attachment decisions.

entries.source_title: Tout/tous/toute/toutes = Everything/all (of them)/whole/completely in French
entries.evidence: Distinguishes agreeing determiner, everything/all pronouns and adverb agreement before feminine consonants versus vowels or mute h.

entries.source_title: Quelqu'un/Quelqu'un d'autre = Someone/Someone else (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Defines unspecified and alternative people, shows reception/help situations and requires both quelqu'un and quelqu'un d'autre.

entries.source_title: Using [French stress pronouns] + même(s) to express "myself/yourself/etc" in French
entries.evidence: Lists the full hyphenated même series and tests singular polite vous, plural vous, elle and nous emphasis.

entries.source_title: Moi/toi/lui/elle/soi/nous/vous/eux/elles - advanced usages (French Stress Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Covers standalone answers, prepositions, identification, emphasis and generic soi; exercises distinguish personal and unspecified reference.

entries.source_title: Y = There (French Adverbial Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Replaces locations including chez a person; tests present, auxiliary, infinitive and negative placement.

entries.source_title: En with quantities = Of them (French Adverbial Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Teaches partitive and counted en, retention of numbers/un/une and quantified people; tests multiple verb positions and negative quantity.

entries.source_title: Autre chose/quelque chose d'autre = Something else (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Explains both something-else expressions and explicitly accepts both in the constrained completion.

entries.source_title: L'autre/Les autres = The other one(s) (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Identified alternatives are taught with a replacement pen and remaining group members; both singular and plural are assessed.

entries.source_title: Expressing quantities in French with quelques/plusieurs/de nombreux = A few/several/many
entries.evidence: Defines all three quantities with plural nouns and explicitly assesses feminine de nombreuses.

entries.source_title: Me becomes moi in affirmative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif) in French
entries.evidence: Affirmative moi contrasts with negative me; the m' elision before en is separately explained and assessed.

entries.source_title: Using object pronouns le/la/les vs lui/leur in affirmative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif) in French
entries.evidence: Command examples preserve direct/indirect roles and hyphens; tasks assess direct objects, recipients and two-pronoun order.

entries.source_title: Chacun/chacune/chaque = each one/each (French Indefinite Adjectives and Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Contrasts chaque plus singular noun with standalone chacun/chacune and singular verb agreement.

entries.source_title: Position of French Object Pronouns - with compound tenses
entries.evidence: Places objects before the auxiliary and distinguishes preceding direct-object agreement from indirect lui.

entries.source_title: Le/la même and Les mêmes = The same (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Defines the agreeing same-one forms and tests feminine singular and plural references.

entries.source_title: Le mien/le tien/le sien/etc = Mine/yours/his/hers/its (French Possessive Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Full mien/tien/sien gender-number matrices distinguish owner from possessed noun; assessments include his feminine and her masculine possessions.

entries.source_title: Le nôtre/le vôtre/le leur/etc = Ours/yours/theirs (French Possessive Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Teaches full nôtre/vôtre/leur forms, circumflexes and contracted articles; each owner series and contraction is assessed.

entries.source_title: N'importe qui = Anyone (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Free-choice anyone contrasts with not just anyone; tasks assess meaning and singular verb agreement.

entries.source_title: N'importe quoi = Nonsense, anything (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Explains unrestricted thing choice and evaluative nonsense in separate examples and assessments.

entries.source_title: Which form of the conjugated verb to pick between nous/vous/ils/elles in cases with multiple subjects (French Subject Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Teaches speaker/addressee/third-person priority and feminine-only groups; all decisions appear in constructed responses.

entries.source_title: Conjugate semi-regular -oyer/-ayer/-uyer verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Complete envoyer/essuyer/payer paradigms explain y retention and optional -ayer i spellings; tests cover all three families.

entries.source_title: Using the infinitive form of verbs to express the English "-ING"
entries.evidence: Distinguishes named activities and second-verb infinitives from a conjugated present action; avoids a universal translation rule for English -ing.

entries.source_title: Conjugate ouvrir/découvrir and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Complete ouvrir paradigm and derivative rule accompany ouvrir/découvrir/recouvrir assessments rather than a finir regularisation.

entries.source_title: Conjugate offrir/souffrir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Lists every present form of both verbs and tests different persons of offrir and souffrir.

entries.source_title: Expressing necessity and obligation in French with "il faut"
entries.evidence: Impersonal il faut takes a noun or infinitive; examples and tests distinguish prohibition from lack of necessity.

entries.source_title: Conjugate cueillir and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Complete cueillir/accueillir patterns extend to recueillir; the three verbs have distinct production items.

entries.source_title: Conjugate savoir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Complete sais/sait/savons/savez/savent paradigm is taught with information and skill contexts and plural/singular retrieval.

entries.source_title: Conjugate connaître/paraître and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Full connaître and paraître forms include reconnaître/apparaître/disparaître; accepted circumflex-free variants remain valid answers.

entries.source_title: Conjugate voir and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Explains voi-/voy- distribution in the full paradigm and assesses voir, revoir and prévoir.

entries.source_title: Conjugate suivre/vivre and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Full vivre/suivre paradigms and survivors/continuing derivatives distinguish meanings and singular versus plural stems.

entries.source_title: Conjugate rire/sourire in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Lists all rire/sourire forms and assesses rions, souriez, rient and sourit in distinct contexts.

entries.source_title: Conjugate servir and other -VIR verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Full servir pattern explains dropping v only in its singular family, with desservir transfer and a warning against overapplying to vivre.

entries.source_title: Conjugate recevoir and other -cevoir verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Teaches all three recevoir stems and transfers to apercevoir, concevoir, décevoir and percevoir with named assessments.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs in -aindre/-eindre/-oindre in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Full craindre/peindre/éteindre/joindre patterns and derivative rules assess every named vowel family and plural gn spelling.

entries.source_title: Conjugate conduire and other -uire verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Full conduire paradigm extends to construire/traduire/réduire; separate cuire/fuir forms prevent a false universal -uire rule.

entries.source_title: Plus que/Moins que/Autant que = More than/Less than/As much as (Comparisons with Verbs in French)
entries.evidence: Compares action amounts with plus/moins/autant que and contrasts equality with adjective/adverb aussi.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular verbs in the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif)
entries.evidence: All tu/nous/vous regular command forms omit the subject; exercises distinguish -er s deletion from finir and attendre.

entries.source_title: Conjugate courir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Full courir paradigm, parcourir transfer and present courons versus future courrons are explicitly taught and assessed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er verbs (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Defines auxiliary and participle, lists all avoir persons and derives -é; tests complete forms without subject agreement.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -ir verbs (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Finir-family -i participles are formed and illustrated; choisir/réussir/remplir assess transfer and infinitive repair.

entries.source_title: Using the French compound past (Le Passé Composé) to express sentences in the English simple past
entries.evidence: Explains completed-event viewpoint and both English simple-past and present-perfect translations; assesses yesterday's completed posting.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -dre verbs (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Regular vendre/attendre/répondre give -u; prendre is explicitly excluded from the regular shortcut.

entries.source_title: Conjugate dire (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Dire has dit within the full avoir paradigm; a name example supports an assessed complete nous form.

entries.source_title: Conjugate faire (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Faire gives fait with avoir; assessments cover vous and elles without incorrect subject agreement.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Separates avoir auxiliary from eu participle using a problem example and tu/je assessed forms.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Explicitly teaches avoir + été and repairs an erroneous être auxiliary rather than inferring auxiliary from the main verb.

entries.source_title: Conjugate coming and going verbs (+ être) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Lists coming/going participles with full être forms and contrasts subject movement with avoir plus a direct object.

entries.source_title: Agreeing past participle with subject's gender and number with (+ être) verbs in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Explains masculine/feminine singular/plural endings, polite vous and reference-sensitive on; assessments specify the referents.

entries.source_title: Conjugate mourir, naître, décéder, devenir, rester (+ être) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: All five named life/change verbs have explicit participles, examples, agreement support and their own assessment item.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs (+être) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Full reflexive auxiliary sequence includes negative placement and contrasts direct se with lavé les mains and indirect se sont parlé.

entries.source_title: Conjugate prendre and derivatives (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Pris/appris/compris/repris are taught as a family with all avoir persons and distinct use contexts.

entries.source_title: Conjugate voir/devoir/pouvoir/boire/croire/savoir/lire/plaire/taire (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: All nine named participles vu/dû/pu/bu/cru/su/lu/plu/tu have explicit meanings, contextual examples and individually identified items.

entries.source_title: Conjugate mettre and derivatives (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Mis/remis/permis/promis/admis are explicitly taught and assessed with the full avoir substitution paradigm.

entries.source_title: Conjugate ouvrir/découvrir and derivatives (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Ouvert/découvert/recouvert are distinguished from present-style or -é regularisation; each verb has its own item.

entries.source_title: Conjugate recevoir and other -cevoir verbs (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: The reçu/aperçu/conçu/déçu/perçu family keeps ç before u; base and derivative forms are assessed independently.

entries.source_title: Conjugate -aindre, -eindre, -oindre verbs (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Explicit -aint/-eint/-oint participles contrast with present plural gn; all three families and useful derivatives are assessed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular verbs in the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.evidence: Present-nous stem formation and all six endings include -iss-, retained i/y and common irregular-present stems.

entries.source_title: Expressing continuing action with the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.evidence: Rain and meal-preparation scenes establish an action already underway; assessment separates that scene from the interrupting event.

entries.source_title: Using the compound tense (Le Passé Composé) on its own or with the imperfect tense (L'Imparfait)
entries.evidence: Explains standalone event sequences, background/event pairing and long but bounded intervals; tasks test each distinction.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être in the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.evidence: Complete étais/était/étions/étiez/étaient forms use the exceptional ét- stem, with plural retrieval and a correction.

entries.source_title: Expressing opinions and describing with the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.evidence: Past setting and trouver opinions are illustrated and assessed, with a warning that bounded reactions can also use passé composé.

entries.source_title: Conjugate semi-regular -cer verbs in the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.evidence: Full commencer paradigm explains ç before a but c before i; commencer and avancer assess both spellings.

entries.source_title: Conjugate semi-regular -ger verbs in the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.evidence: Full manger paradigm keeps e before a and removes it before i; manger/changer/voyager have separate forms assessed.

entries.source_title: Expressing past habits or repeated actions with the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.evidence: Open-ended habits are contrasted with counted completed repetitions so frequency alone does not mechanically select the tense.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs in the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.evidence: Full se lever paradigm retains reflexive pronouns before one imparfait verb, without an être auxiliary.

entries.source_title: Conjugate conduire and other -uire verbs in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Conduit/construit/produit/traduit/réduit follow an explicit -uit participle family rather than present plural -s- stems.

entries.source_title: Conjugate tenir and derivatives (+avoir) in the French compound past (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Tenu/obtenu/retenu/maintenu/soutenu are explicitly identified with avoir; four family members have individual retrieval items.

entries.source_title: Conjugate suivre (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Full avoir + suivi paradigm and poursuivre transfer use a course and continuing-discussion contexts.

entries.source_title: Conjugate écrire and derivatives (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Écrit/décrit/inscrit/réécrit retain their final t; each named family form has contextual assessment.

entries.source_title: Conjugate offrir and souffrir (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Offert and souffert are distinguished from present-like regularisation and each has its own complete past-form item.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vivre (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Vécu and survivre's survécu take avoir; the example and assessment distinguish lived from voir's vu.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Voulu with avoir includes the negative refusal reading and a warning that wanting does not guarantee success.

entries.source_title: Monter dans, descendre de = To get on, off transportation in French (prepositions)
entries.evidence: Entering a vehicle uses monter dans; getting off uses descendre de with article contractions and an onto-surface contrast.

entries.source_title: Using the present tense (Le Présent) - and not the compound past (Le Passé Composé) - in sentences with "depuis" (since/for) in French (French Prepositions of Time)
entries.evidence: Present plus depuis describes a continuing situation; explicit completed-event and negative-event counterexamples prevent the heading becoming a false blanket rule.

entries.source_title: After/before versus in front of/behind (French Prepositions of Time and Place)
entries.evidence: Earlier/later events contrast with physical front/behind locations, with all four prepositions separately assessed.

entries.source_title: Expressing for + [duration] in French with either pendant/durant/depuis/pour (French Prepositions of Time)
entries.evidence: Ongoing elapsed duration, bounded intervals and intended booking periods determine depuis, pendant/durant or pour; both interval synonyms are accepted.

entries.source_title: En vs Dans with time (French Prepositions of Time)
entries.evidence: Time required for completion contrasts with a delay before a future event; repair, ferry and cooking tasks specify the timeline.

entries.source_title: Aimer = to love, like something/someone in French
entries.evidence: Aimer with things, activities and people includes the non-intensifying aimer bien distinction and direct infinitive complements.

entries.source_title: Expressing "to find" and opinions with the verb "trouver" in French
entries.evidence: Literal discovery contrasts with object-adjective and trouver que opinions; tests assess meaning, agreement and clause introduction.

entries.source_title: "Sentir bon" vs "Se sentir bien" - The different meanings of the verb "sentir" in French
entries.evidence: Full sentir and reflexive forms contrast sensing an object, smelling good and feeling well; tests also separate invariable bon from agreeing adjectives.

entries.source_title: Avoir raison/tort/de la chance = To be right/wrong/lucky (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.evidence: All three expressions use avoir rather than an English-shaped être; present and past examples support separate assessments.

entries.source_title: Expressing you like something/someone in French with the verb "plaire"
entries.evidence: The liked thing controls plaire and the experiencer is indirect; full forms and perspective-changing tasks include accepted plaît/plait spellings.

entries.source_title: Aller à = to suit someone (French Expressions with aller)
entries.evidence: Aller expresses clothing fit and suitable arrangements, not movement; singular time and plural shoes are assessed.

entries.source_title: Visiter vs Rendre visite à whether you visit a place or a person
entries.evidence: Places use visiter; ordinary social visits use rendre visite à, while professional/institutional personal visiter is not universally rejected.

entries.source_title: Connaître vs savoir = to know something vs to know how to do in French
entries.evidence: Familiarity, known information and infinitive skills select different constructions; knowing a memorised text prevents an overbroad no-noun rule.

entries.source_title: Expressing "to walk" with se promener/promener/marcher/aller à pied in French
entries.evidence: Walking activity, transport on foot, strolling and taking an animal out each receive explanations, examples and individual items.

entries.source_title: Using manquer (à) to say you miss someone or something emotionally in French
entries.evidence: The missed person or thing is the subject; examples and transformations test experiencer pronouns, reversal and subject agreement.

entries.source_title: Using manquer (de) to say you/something miss or lack in French
entries.evidence: Distinguishes missed direct-object events, lack of resources, missing items, failed obligations and nearly doing something.

entries.source_title: Avoir honte de = to be ashamed of (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.evidence: Defines avoir honte de with a mistake example and assesses the required preposition.

entries.source_title: Faire exprès (de) = To do something on purpose (French Expressions with faire)
entries.evidence: Faire exprès de introduces deliberate action; negation denies intention, not necessarily the event, with both form and meaning assessed.

entries.source_title: Faire mal à vs Faire du mal à = to hurt someone (French Expressions with faire)
entries.evidence: Pain contrasts with broader harm, explicitly allowing physical harm with du mal; tasks assess subject agreement, article and scope.

entries.source_title: Il y a + [durée] = [duration] + ago (French Expressions of Time)
entries.evidence: Il y a dates a completed event before now, distinct from a duration or existential there is; two event contexts test it.

entries.source_title: Faire peur (à) = To scare someone (French Expressions with faire)
entries.evidence: A noise is the frightening subject and affected children are introduced with à/leur; the assessment replaces the indirect experiencer.

entries.source_title: Faire la queue = To queue/To be in line/To stand in line (French Expressions with faire)
entries.evidence: Teaches waiting in line with faire la queue, full faire forms and the accepted Canadian faire la file alternative.

entries.source_title: Expressing timeliness in French - late/early - precise
entries.evidence: Separates tôt/tard clock timing from en avance/en retard/à l'heure and quantified minutes d'avance/de retard.

entries.source_title: Se souvenir de/Se rappeler (de) = To remember something in French
entries.evidence: Full memory-verb paradigms and direct/de contrasts include OQLF-supported personal-pronoun and reminder-infinitive de exceptions, not a blanket ban.

entries.source_title: Faire partie de = To be part of (French Expressions with faire)
entries.evidence: Belonging uses faire partie de with final e; items assess the preposition and de + le contraction.

entries.source_title: Expressing ongoing actions in the past in French: être en train de
entries.evidence: Être in the imparfait plus en train de and an infinitive emphasises an ongoing past activity without making it obligatory for every English progressive.

entries.source_title: Faire confiance (à) = To trust (French Expressions with faire)
entries.evidence: Trust takes faire confiance à, illustrated with an organisation and assessed with a personal complement.

entries.source_title: Using "devoir" in the imperfect tense versus the compound past in French (L'Imparfait vs Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Complete devais/ai dû paradigms distinguish background obligations, realised necessity and inference without treating every obligation as fulfilled.

entries.source_title: Avoir l'habitude de = To be in the habit of, to tend to (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.evidence: Avoir l'habitude de plus infinitive describes present or past habits; assessments retrieve the full present expression and past auxiliary.

entries.source_title: Demi/moitié/etc = Half in French
entries.evidence: Contrasts invariant pre-noun demi-, gender-only et demi(e), la moitié de and adverbial à moitié, including midi.

entries.source_title: S'en aller = To leave in French
entries.evidence: Complete present and passé composé s'en aller paradigms preserve en, explain departure versus destination and assess negative placement.

entries.source_title: Common mistakes with mon/ma/mes, ton/ta/tes and son/sa/ses (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.evidence: The full owner/noun matrix separates owner's identity from possessed noun gender and number, with deliberately contrasting male/female owners.

entries.source_title: "Ma" becomes "mon" with feminine nouns starting with a vowel or mute h (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.evidence: Vowel/mute-h feminine nouns take mon/ton/son; an intervening consonant-starting adjective restores the feminine form.

entries.source_title: Bien, mal, mieux, moins, peu (Irregular French Adverbs)
entries.evidence: All five adverbs have explicit meanings and contextual examples; each is assessed, with bien versus bon and mieux versus plus bien.

entries.source_title: Ce/cet/cette and ces = this/that and these/those (French Demonstrative Adjectives)
entries.evidence: All four demonstratives are selected by noun gender/number and masculine initial sound, with this/that scope and -ci/-là clarification.

entries.source_title: Forming adverbs from adjectives ending in a vowel in French (French Adverbs)
entries.evidence: Vowel-ending poli/vrai/absolu/aisé form adverbs without the usual feminine e; tasks assess the retained masculine base.

entries.source_title: Position of French Adverbs - general rule
entries.evidence: Explains post-verbal manner/amount position, pre-adjective modifiers and flexible time/place placement; the task specifies its intended placement.

entries.source_title: Special cases when you use mon/ma/mes/etc with parts of the body (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.evidence: Contrasts pronoun-established body ownership with independent descriptive or emphatic possessives; both choices are assessed in specified contexts.

entries.source_title: Forming the feminine of adjectives ending in -f in French
entries.evidence: Feminine f-to-ve family includes neuf/actif/sportif/vif/veuf and the accent-changing bref caution; assessments include plural agreement.

entries.source_title: Plus ... que/Moins ... que/Aussi ... que = More ... than/Less ... than/As ... as (Comparisons with Adjectives in French)
entries.evidence: Adjective comparison retains agreement and contrasts plus/moins/aussi with verb autant; meilleur supplies the common bon exception.

entries.source_title: Adjectives after personne, rien, tout le monde, quelqu'un are always masculine in French
entries.evidence: Teaches generic masculine singular indefinite patterns and de before adjectives, while distinguishing feminine noun une personne and context-sensitive personal agreement.

entries.source_title: Forming adverbs from adjectives ending in -ant and -ent in French (French Adverbs)
entries.evidence: Explains -amment/-emment spellings and shared sound, plus lent/présent exceptions; tasks retrieve both families and lentement.

entries.source_title: Plus ... que/Moins ... que/Aussi ... que = More ... than/Less ... than/As ... as (Comparisons with Adverbs in French)
entries.evidence: Invariable manner adverbs use plus/moins/aussi ... que; equality and comparison-link words are assessed.

entries.source_title: D'autres vs des autres = others (French Indefinite Adjectives)
entries.evidence: Unspecified additional items use d'autres; possession requiring de + les autres gives des autres; both are contrasted and assessed.

entries.source_title: Forming the feminine of adjectives ending in -c in French
entries.evidence: Blanche/franche/sèche/publique/turque/grecque/caduque are individually taught and assessed rather than forced into one ending rule.

entries.source_title: Position of French Adverbs - with compound tenses
entries.evidence: Short adverbs commonly separate auxiliary and participle; longer manner adverbs follow the participle or object, with specified-position tasks.

entries.source_title: Forming the feminine of adjectives ending in -oux + "faux" in French
entries.evidence: Full doux/douce, roux/rousse, jaloux/jalouse and faux/fausse gender-number sets each have an assessment.

entries.source_title: De plus en plus / De moins en moins + [adverbe/adjectif/verbe] = more and more / less and less + [adverb/adjective/verb] (Comparisons in French)
entries.evidence: Increasing/decreasing trends precede adjectives/adverbs or follow verbs; tasks independently assess all three placements.

entries.source_title: Frais, long, favori, rigolo have irregular feminine forms (French adjectives)
entries.evidence: Full frais/long/favori/rigolo gender-number sets include fraîche/fraiche variants and the informal register of rigolo; each is assessed.

entries.source_title: Using son/sa/ses to express possession with personne/tout le monde/chacun/il faut (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.evidence: Generic singular owners use son/sa/ses according to the possessed noun; examples include chacun and assessments include tout le monde, il faut and personne.

entries.source_title: Using notre/nos versus son/sa/ses with "on" depending on its meaning (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.evidence: Identified conversational we contrasts with generic people; explicitly specified ownership makes notre versus sa answers fair.

entries.source_title: Quel/quelle/quels/quelles + [nom] = What a [noun] (French Exclamative Adjectives)
entries.evidence: Exclamative quel agrees with the noun and omits English-shaped un/une; singular and plural exclamations are assessed.

entries.source_title: Le plus/Le moins = The most/the least (Superlative with Adverbs in French)
entries.evidence: Adverb superlatives retain invariable le even with feminine subjects; the tasks construct fastest and most clearly.

entries.source_title: Le plus/Le moins = The most/the least (Superlative with Verbs in French)
entries.evidence: Le plus/le moins follow a verb to rank action amounts, unlike adjective agreement; a least-driving comparison is assessed.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas du tout = Not at all (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Du tout strengthens the negative denial; a complete transformation requires the full ne ... pas du tout construction.

entries.source_title: Ne ... plus = No more/no longer (French Negations)
entries.evidence: A formerly true situation ends with ne ... plus, without additional pas; work and transport transformations assess that timeline.

entries.source_title: Ne ... personne = No one/nobody (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Personne acts as subject or object; compound placement after the participle and retained verbal prepositions are separately assessed.

entries.source_title: Ne ... rien = Nothing (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Rien as subject precedes ne; as compound-tense object it usually precedes the participle. Both constructions have full-sentence tasks.

entries.source_title: Position of French Object Pronouns - with negations
entries.evidence: Explains ne before the pronoun group and pas after the conjugated verb/auxiliary, while keeping an infinitive's object with that infinitive.

entries.source_title: N'avoir plus de = To have none left (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Exhausted supplies use ne ... plus de/d'; money and ticket contexts test elision and the negative quantity article.

entries.source_title: Using restrictive ne … que to express only with simple tenses (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Only is a restriction, not ordinary negation; que directly precedes its scope, elides before a vowel and retains the positive article.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas non plus = Not ... either (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Non plus adds another negative rather than intensifying it; the item completes a second negative response.

entries.source_title: Ne ... aucun(e) = None (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Aucun/aucune normally introduces a singular noun directly and can be subject or object; plural-only noun exceptions are acknowledged.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas assez (de) = Not enough (of) (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Insufficient noun quantities require de while insufficient adjective degree does not; the two constructions are contrasted in assessment.

entries.source_title: Ne ... ni ... ni = Neither ... nor (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Two exclusions use ne ... ni ... ni; unspecified quantities omit partitives whereas definite preferences retain their articles.

entries.source_title: Forming simple negative commands with the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif)
entries.evidence: Negative imperatives retain ne ... pas and restore before-verb me/te/le forms, without affirmative hyphens.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas = Not - with compound tenses (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Ne and pas surround the auxiliary, with full avoir and être sentence transformations.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas grand-chose = Not ... much (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Pas grand-chose means a small amount rather than necessarily nothing; meaning and hyphenated form are assessed.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas encore = Not yet (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Pas encore expresses an expected event not yet realised and follows the auxiliary in compound tenses.

entries.source_title: Quel/quels/quelle/quelles ? = Which/what? (French Question Words)
entries.evidence: All four quel forms agree with the selected noun, including separated identification with être; tasks specify gender and number.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the present tense (Le Présent) in French - regular forms (except il/elle/on forms)
entries.evidence: Pronoun inversion uses verb-hyphen-subject; regular persons and a non-inverted est-ce que alternative are taught and assessed.

entries.source_title: Que + [inverted statement] ? = What ... ? (French Questions)
entries.evidence: Que represents an unknown thing as object before inversion, illustrated with searching a file and assessed with vouloir.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the present tense (Le Présent) in French - il/elle/on forms
entries.evidence: Vowel-ending forms need linking -t-; existing d/t remain without extra t. Items contrast arrive-t-elle, va-t-on and prend-elle.

entries.source_title: Qui/Qui est-ce qui [conjugated verb] ? = Who ... ? (French Questions)
entries.evidence: The unknown person is the subject, requiring qui or qui est-ce qui without an extra subject; present and past tasks assess it.

entries.source_title: Qui/Qui est-ce que ... ? = Whom ... ? (French Questions)
entries.evidence: Unknown personal objects use qui with inversion or qui est-ce que; required verbal prepositions are retained.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions with reflexive verbs in the present tense (Le Présent) in French
entries.evidence: Reflexive pronouns stay before the verb while subject pronouns move after it; tu and repeated vous constructions are assessed.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the compound past (Le Passé Composé) in French - with subject pronouns
entries.evidence: Only the auxiliary inverts in compound questions; avoir and être examples and tasks keep the participle in place.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the present tense (Le Présent) in French - with names/things/emphasis
entries.evidence: Complex inversion retains a name/noun and repeats it with a matching pronoun; assessments cover plural things and a named person.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the present tense (Le Présent) in French - special cases "puis-je/ai-je/suis-je"
entries.evidence: All three special je inversion forms are explained and assessed; ordinary est-ce que alternatives and the limits of generalising je inversion are explicit.

entries.source_title: Qu'est-ce qui + [conjugated verb] = What [does]... (French Questions)
entries.evidence: Qu'est-ce qui identifies a thing as grammatical subject; happening and blocking questions assess construction without an extra il.

entries.source_title: Using "une dizaine" and other approximate numbers in French
entries.evidence: Approximate-number nouns from dizaine through millier take de; a packaged douzaine can be exactly twelve rather than always approximate.

entries.source_title: Prochain/Dernier = Next/Last + [durations] in French
entries.evidence: Calendar-relative next/last normally follows the period; sequence selection and la prochaine fois use preceding position, with noun agreement.

entries.source_title: Expressing intervals of dates and times in French = from ... to ...
entries.evidence: De ... à time intervals contrast with du ... au date/weekday contractions; each interval type is assessed.

entries.source_title: Doing arithmetic in French - addition, subtraction, multiplication, division
entries.evidence: Each of plus, moins, fois/multiplié par and divisé par is explained with a correct calculation and assessed operation or result.

entries.source_title: Some plural English nouns are singular in French and vice versa
entries.evidence: French singular garments contrast with plural vacances, cheveux, conseils and renseignements; items test actual French number rather than English countability.

entries.source_title: De plus en plus de / de moins en moins de + [nom] = more and more / less and less + [nouns] (Comparisons in French)
entries.evidence: Increasing/decreasing noun quantities require final de, unlike adjective/adverb/verb trends; both directions have constructed items.

entries.source_title: Forming the plural of French nouns ending in -ou
entries.evidence: The ordinary -ous rule contrasts with all seven bijoux/cailloux/choux/genoux/hiboux/joujoux/poux exceptions; each exception and a regular noun are assessed.

entries.source_title: Some French nouns have different meanings depending on whether they're masculine or feminine
entries.evidence: Article-labelled livre/tour/manche/mode/poste/voile/poêle pairs demonstrate distinct meanings, with noun-specific article assessments and further moule/mémoire reference pairs.
